features: Login with email/password returning JWT for session authentication
Enforce manager vs. member permissions for project and task actions
Create, read, update, and delete projects with name and description

user_stories.want: to create a new project
acceptance_criteria: A logged‑in manager sees a "Create Project" button on the dashboard
Submitting a name and description creates a project record and returns its ID
The new project appears in the manager's project list immediately

user_stories.want: to delete a project
acceptance_criteria: The Delete button is visible only to users with the manager role on that project
Confirming deletion removes the project and all its tasks from the database
The deleted project no longer appears in any user's project list

user_stories.want: to add a member to a project with a specific role
acceptance_criteria: Manager can search for existing users by email and assign them as "manager" or "member"
The invited user appears in the project's member list with the selected role
An email invitation (or in‑app notification) is sent after the assignment

user_stories.want: to view all tasks within a project
acceptance_criteria: Member can navigate to a project and see a list of its tasks showing title, due date, and status
Tasks displayed belong only to the selected project
Edit and Delete controls are not visible to members

user_stories.want: to update a task's status
acceptance_criteria: Member can change the status dropdown from "todo" to "in_progress" or "done"
The new status is persisted and reflected after a page refresh
A timestamp of the status change is stored (verified via API response)

user_stories.want: to edit task details (title, description, due date)
acceptance_criteria: Manager can open an edit form, modify fields, and save
All changed fields are saved and returned correctly by the API
The system rejects a due date that is in the past with a validation error

user_stories.want: to delete a task
acceptance_criteria: Delete button appears only for managers on a task detail view
After confirmation, the task record is removed from the database
The task no longer appears in the project's task list

user_stories.want: to log in securely
acceptance_criteria: Providing valid email and password returns a JWT token
All subsequent API calls require a valid JWT or return 401 Unauthorized
Invalid credentials result in a 401 response with an error message

user_stories.want: to view the project's member list with roles
acceptance_criteria: Project page displays a table of members showing name, email, and role
Roles are correctly labeled as "manager" or "member"
The list updates instantly after adding or removing a member

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — all endpoints must verify JWT
non_functional_requirements.authorization: role‑based: managers can delete projects/members, members have read‑only access to project data

non_functional_requirements.search: required on /users endpoint for member lookup

blog_cms.idea: A blog CMS with author and reader roles. Authors write posts with title, content (markdown), tags, and cover image URL. Posts can be saved as draft or published. Readers see all published posts, can f

api_endpoints.description: Populates database with realistic demo data.
Returns aggregate counts and key metrics for the dashboard.
Authenticates a user and returns a JWT token.
Retrieves the profile of the currently authenticated user.
Retrieves a paginated list of all published blog posts, with optional tag filtering.
Retrieves a single published blog post by its ID.
Retrieves a paginated list of posts by a specific author, including drafts for the author themselves.
Creates a new blog post (initially as a draft).
Updates an existing blog post by its ID.
Publishes a draft post, making it visible to readers.
Unpublishes a published post, making it a draft again.
Deletes a blog post by its ID.
Retrieves a list of all available tags.
Creates a new tag (admin/author only).
Deletes a tag (admin/author only).

features: Secure login for authors and role-based access control to ensure authors can only manage their own posts and readers can only view published content.
Authors can create new posts with title, markdown content, tags, and a cover image URL, and edit existing posts.
Authors can save posts as drafts for later editing and explicitly publish them when ready, making them visible to readers.
Authors can delete their own posts, removing them from the system.
Readers can view a list of all published posts, displaying title, author, date, and tags.
Readers can filter the list of published posts by selecting one or more tags.
Readers can click on a post to view its full content, including rendered markdown, title, author, date, tags, and cover image.

user_stories.want: to create a new blog post
acceptance_criteria: I can input a title, markdown content, tags, and a cover image URL.
The post is saved as a 'draft' by default upon creation.
I receive confirmation that my post has been successfully created.

user_stories.want: to save a post as a draft
acceptance_criteria: When I save a post, its status is set to 'draft'.
Draft posts are not visible to readers.
I can access and edit my draft posts from my author dashboard.

user_stories.want: to publish a draft post
acceptance_criteria: I can change the status of a draft post to 'published'.
The published post immediately appears in the list of posts visible to readers.
The published post displays its title, my name, the publication date, and its tags.

user_stories.want: to edit an existing post (draft or published)
acceptance_criteria: I can modify the title, content, tags, and cover image URL of any of my posts.
If the post is published, the changes are reflected immediately for readers.
I receive confirmation that my post has been successfully updated.

user_stories.want: to view a list of all published blog posts
acceptance_criteria: I see a list of posts, each displaying its title, author, publication date, and tags.
Only 'published' posts are visible in this list.
The list is ordered by publication date, newest first.

user_stories.want: to filter posts by a specific tag
acceptance_criteria: I can select a tag to filter the post list.
Only posts containing the selected tag are displayed.
The filter can be cleared to show all published posts again.

user_stories.want: to read a full blog post
acceptance_criteria: When I click on a post title, I am taken to a dedicated page for that post.
The full content (markdown rendered), title, author, publication date, and cover image are displayed.
The post's tags are also visible on the individual post page.

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — Authors need to log in to manage posts; Readers do not need to log in to view posts.
non_functional_requirements.authorization: Authors can only create, edit, delete, and publish their own posts. Readers can only view published posts.
non_functional_requirements.pagination: required on: /posts (for readers), /authors/{author_id}/posts (for authors)

The driver receives a rejection notification with an optional reason.
The rejected request is still visible in the driver’s trip history with status "rejected".

user_stories.want: to log a maintenance record for a vehicle
acceptance_criteria: A maintenance record is created when date, description, and cost are provided.
The vehicle status automatically switches to "maintenance" for the maintenance date range.
The total maintenance cost for a vehicle can be retrieved via a summary endpoint.

user_stories.want: to view my trip history
acceptance_criteria: The trip history endpoint returns only trips belonging to the authenticated driver.
Each trip entry includes vehicle details, dates, purpose, and final status.
Results are paginated with a default page size of 20.

user_stories.want: to view total maintenance cost per vehicle
acceptance_criteria: A summary endpoint returns vehicle_id, license_plate, and sum(cost) of all maintenance records.
The endpoint filters out vehicles with no maintenance records.
The response is sorted descending by total cost.

user_stories.want: to see which vehicles are currently available
acceptance_criteria: The vehicle list endpoint returns only vehicles with status "available" for the requested date range.
Search parameters (license_plate, make) filter the list correctly.
Pagination is applied with a maximum of 50 items per page.

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required - all endpoints must be accessed by an authenticated user to protect fleet data.

non_functional_requirements.file_uploads: no - maintenance records are textual only.
non_functional_requirements.real_time: no - updates are reflected on next API call; real‑time push not needed.

acceptance_criteria: POST /transactions with type='purchase' updates product.current_stock = previous + quantity

Response includes the updated product stock value

user_stories.want: to record a sale
acceptance_criteria: POST /transactions with type='sale' reduces product.current_stock by quantity

acceptance_criteria: GET /dashboard returns a list of products where current_stock < reorder_threshold

user_stories.want: to edit product details
acceptance_criteria: PATCH /products/{id} updates allowed fields and returns 200 with the updated product
